clue.text: Gull abroad having shortened tail

parts.note: abroad means out, away from home

indicators.note: shortened tail says the last letter of the word for having is cut off

parts.note: having means with, as in a man with a hat

explanation.surface: A seagull overseas has lost part of its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe or trick them, getting the better of them by cunning.

clue.text: Start of an attack

explanation.surface: The opening moment of an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of anything is its onset, and an onset is also an old word for an assault or charge.

clue.text: Cover-up of defeat

explanation.surface: Hiding a heavy loss from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash conceals faults like paint over a stain, and in sport it is a crushing win where the loser takes nothing.

clue.text: Threat to health from low tars?

definitions.text: Threat to health from low tars?

parts.words: Threat to health from low tars?
parts.note: reads like a warning about low-tar cigarettes, but tars are sailors and the threat comes from low down, under the waterline, to their ship

explanation.surface: A health warning about low-tar cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater weapon strikes a vessel below the waterline, endangering the sailors aboard.

clue.text: Her majesty's house?

parts.note: suggests a royal palace, but a house is the people in a theatre and the Queen grants a formal meeting of the same name

explanation.surface: A question about where the monarch lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's house is the assembled spectators, and a formal interview with the monarch is also called by this name.

clue.text: Complaint after a new statute

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the preceding words are made into something fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A grievance raised after a law is freshly passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns the fifteen letters of COMPLAINT AFTER A into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A law passed by the UK legislature is formally a statute enacted by Lords and Commons.

clue.text: Firm turning over Italian island, mostly rough

indicators.note: turning over says the whole string formed by the following pieces is read from the end back

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled

indicators.note: mostly says the word for rough loses its final letter

parts.note: rough means rude, as in crude or unpolished

explanation.surface: A company capsizing off an Italian island in rough seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses ELBA + RUD (RUDE without its last letter, from 'mostly'), giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is sturdy and long-lasting, built to stand up to wear.

clue.text: Lose nothing, rebuilding pontoons without a break

indicators.note: rebuilding says the remaining letters are reassembled in a new order
Lose tells us one letter is dropped from the word pontoons before the rest is reworked

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Engineers rebuilding floating bridges around the clock without losing anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose' removes one O from PONTOONS, leaving PONTONS, and 'rebuilding' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Working without a break means continuing without pause or interruption.

clue.text: …or make a threat to wife in this place, or another

parts.note: or else! is a classic threat, the ellipsis and the leading or setting it up
in this place means here

explanation.surface: A threat to a wife, linked to some earlier sentence by the ellipsis.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from another with an ellipsis; 'or else' is the threat, and the definition 'or another' means in a place other than this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere other than here is any different location, another spot entirely.

clue.text: Older Spaniard embraces one

indicators.note: embraces says the word for a Spaniard wraps round the other piece

parts.note: senor is the Spanish title for a man, used for a Spaniard
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An elderly Spanish man hugging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder of two people is the more advanced in years, the senior one.

clue.text: Better half deprived of final point

indicators.note: half here takes the second part of the word Better, its last three letters

parts.note: deprived of means minus, without

explanation.surface: A spouse left without the last word in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' looks like a spouse, but it asks for half of BETTER, TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end of a line or route, its final stop.

clue.text: Like one fated, cruelly, to have no ear?

definitions.text: Like one fated, cruelly, to have no ear?

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters of the previous words are treated roughly, jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone doomed by fate never to hear music properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' rearranges ONE FATED; the whole clue describes someone with no ear for music.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no ear for music means being unable to tell pitches apart.

clue.text: Present most excellent ring to wife

parts.note: the most excellent thing is the best
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Giving a wife the finest ring as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to give or confer something, as a gift or honour.

clue.text: State of the musical?

explanation.surface: Asking which US state a famous show is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a US state in the Great Plains and the title of the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show.

clue.text: Old-fashioned mechanic who could help in gear selection?

definitions.text: who could help in gear selection?

parts.note: something old-fashioned is out of date, simply out
a fitter is a mechanic who assembles machine parts

explanation.surface: An old mechanic who might help someone change gear in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear selection' suggests a car's gearbox; gear here is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing is often called gear, and a shop supplying clothes helps customers choose it.

clue.text: Slip by England's opener, run out

indicators.note: opener takes the first letter of the word England's, like a batting opener

parts.note: a slip is a lapse, a small mistake

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: England's opening batsman caught at slip, then run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: slip is a fielding position and an opener is a first batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: When time has run out it has passed by completely, gone.

clue.text: Bearing dignitary, fit to fly

parts.note: bearing means manner or air, as in a regal air
a worthy is a notable, important person

explanation.surface: An important official certifying an aircraft safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft certified safe for flight is in a condition fit to take off.

clue.text: At the end one is desperate to restrain an animal

definitions.text: At the end one is desperate to restrain an animal

parts.words: At the end one is desperate to restrain an animal
parts.note: plays on the idiom for being desperate, at the end of one's rope, and on the line used to tie a grazing beast

explanation.surface: A farmer in despair trying to hold a beast back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope tying a grazing animal to a post, and its end is where one has no patience left.

clue.text: One who does in a package

definitions.text: One who does in a package

parts.words: One who does in a package
parts.note: sounds like a killer disposing of a body in a parcel, but does means visits, as in doing Europe on a package holiday

explanation.surface: A murderer hiding a victim in a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker on an all-in trip does the sights abroad.

clue.text: Breather can be especially short in ceremony

indicators.note: in places the abbreviated piece inside the word for a ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
esp is the short form of especially

explanation.surface: A short rest during a solemn ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause for rest, a break from effort.

clue.text: Being scholarly, retitle a novel

indicators.note: novel signals the letters of the preceding words are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A learned author giving a book a fresh title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but rearranges RETITLE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to read and write well, with learning, makes someone educated and lettered.

clue.text: Place name of common man, carrying £25 to a bookie

indicators.note: carrying says the word for the common man holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Tom, as in Tom, Dick and Harry, stands for any ordinary man
a pony is British betting slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: An ordinary man taking a small sum to place a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for £25, used by bookmakers (betting-shop owners).
explanation.definitionFit: A word that names a geographical location, from the Greek for place and name.

clue.text: I go on nights in France to see people from Alaska, possibly

indicators.note: go on says the letter I is placed on, in front of, the next piece

parts.note: nuits is French for nights

explanation.surface: Travelling by night across France to meet Alaskans.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic peoples of Alaska, Canada and Greenland, once called Eskimos.

clue.text: Offer a very soft food fish

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft
the roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Serving up a delicate fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach someone with a proposal is to make an overture or offer.

clue.text: Its eastern dishes can not be taken out

definitions.text: Its eastern dishes can not be taken out

parts.words: Its eastern dishes can not be taken out
parts.note: reads like a restaurant with no takeaway, but dishes are attractive women kept secluded in an eastern household

explanation.surface: An oriental restaurant that does no takeaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a traditional Muslim household, where wives and concubines lived secluded.

clue.text: Aneurin, French friend of yours, once, is outside!

indicators.note: is outside says the archaic word for yours sits round the French piece

parts.note: thine is the old form of yours
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A Welshman named Aneurin and his French friend waiting outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Aneurin looks like a Welsh name (Aneurin Bevan) but is an old name for vitamin B1.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin B1 was formerly known by this other name.

clue.text: Name and number below

parts.note: ether numbs, so it is a number, something that deadens feeling

explanation.surface: A name and a figure written underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er: an anaesthetic that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word for lower or underneath, as in nether regions.

clue.text: Reserved novel, keeping it back

indicators.note: keeping says the word for novel holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: something novel is new, recent

indicators.note: back says the word it is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A shy book that keeps something to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IT into TI, which 'keeping' puts inside RECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is quiet and holds back from speaking freely.

clue.text: Hawthorn border in chaos

parts.note: may is another name for hawthorn blossom
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A hawthorn hedge running riot along the edge of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder and confusion, utter turmoil.
